entities.summary:
Bálint Alsáni was a Hungarian Cardinal, who served as the Bishop of Pécs in the Kingdom of Hungary from 1374 to his death in 1408.

Alsáni played a crucial role in the ecclesiastical politics of the Kingdom of Hungary during the late 14th century. He was a key figure in the Hungarian Catholic Church's relations with the Holy Roman Empire.

Alsáni's tenure as Bishop of Pécs was marked by his efforts to promote the interests of the Hungarian nobility and the Catholic Church in the region. He was also involved in the administration of the diocese, overseeing the construction of various churches and monasteries.

Alsáni's legacy can be seen in the continued importance of the Catholic Church in Hungarian society, as well as his role in shaping the country's political and cultural landscape.

"The Church is the true foundation of the state," Alsáni once said, highlighting the close ties between the ecclesiastical and secular authorities in medieval Hungary.

Born in an unknown location, Alsáni died on November 28, 1408.

entities.summary: Bálint Alsáni was a Hungarian Cardinal who played a pivotal role in the Kingdom of Hungary's ecclesiastical and political landscape during the 14th century. As the Bishop of Pécs from 1374 until his death in 1408, he navigated the complexities of the Catholic Church's influence in medieval Europe, managing to maintain his position as a key advisor to the Hungarian royal court while also contributing to the development of the Hungarian Reformation. Alsáni's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his efforts to promote the interests of the Hungarian people and his advocacy for the rights of the Catholic Church continue to shape the country's history and identity. The cardinal's life and accomplishments have been the subject of various historical accounts, including those of the Hungarian historian Pál Váray, who sought to rehabilitate Alsáni's reputation in the centuries following his death. Through his work, Alsáni helped to secure the position of the Catholic Church in Hungary and paved the way for future generations of Hungarian leaders to navigate the complex web of religious and political intrigue that defined the region during the Middle Ages. Alsáni's remarkable story is one of perseverance, diplomacy, and a commitment to the principles of his faith, making him a fascinating figure in the history of medieval Hungary.
